\section{Introduction and research questions}

%% trace: RQ-P1
\paragraph{RQ-P1.} How does AI assistance affect self-reported cognitive load (fatigue probes, stuck episodes, TLX debrief)?

%% trace: RQ-P2
\paragraph{RQ-P2.} How does AI assistance affect the static cognitive-load profile of the code produced (9-metric matrix over workspace snapshots)?

%% trace: RQ-P3
\paragraph{RQ-P3.} How does AI assistance change working behavior - pasting, file switching, edit provenance, active vs idle time?

%% trace: RQ-P4
\paragraph{RQ-P4.} How do developers review AI-generated code before accepting it (review latency, scroll coverage, accept rate by suggestion size)?

%% trace: RQ-P5
\paragraph{RQ-P5.} How does the conversation with the agent unfold over a session - turn cadence, tool-call mix, reliance loops - and how does it relate to outcomes?

\section{Methodology}

%% trace: FR-PROT-1 / participants
We plan 6 participants in a within-subjects, counterbalanced design across the conditions ai-assisted, unassisted.

%% trace: FR-PROT-1 / session
Each session lasts 45 minutes. Two matched Python maintenance tasks (one per condition, order counterbalanced with condition pairing per the runbook's Latin square): Task A "expenses" and Task B "logbook", each a small existing codebase with two seeded defects and one feature request, shipped with acceptance tests providing outcome ground truth (FR-INST-16, via the task harness). In ai-assisted sessions the participant uses Claude Code in the integrated terminal; in unassisted sessions AI tooling is disabled.

\subsection{Instruments}

%% trace: FR-INST-1 / FR-INST-2 / tern
TERN samples fatigue every 15 minutes (after a 4-second typing pause) and detects stuck episodes after 90 seconds of inactivity (FR-INST-1/2).

%% trace: FR-AGENT-2 / FR-AGENT-5 / agentCapture
In the AI condition the agent interaction is captured via claude-code under a metadata-only content policy (FR-AGENT-2/5).

\subsection{Static code metrics (cognitive-load-9)}
%% trace: FR-INST-4 / metrics
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
Metric & Definition & Source \\
\midrule
Nesting penalty & weighted count of nested control structures & \citep{nejmeh1988} \\
Cognitive complexity & SonarSource cognitive-complexity score & \citep{campbell2018} \\
Parameter count & arity vs Miller's 7+/-2 working-memory bound & \citep{miller1956} \\
Halstead effort & Halstead's effort measure over operators/operands & \citep{halstead1977} \\
Scope distance & mean lines between a name's definition and use & \citep{nejmeh1988} \\
Indentation variance & variance of leading-whitespace depth per file & \citep{hindle2008} \\
Line width & mean/bounded source line length & \citep{hindle2008} \\
Identifier length & mean identifier character length & \citep{lawrie2006} \\
Comment ratio & comment lines / source lines & \citep{nejmeh1988} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\section{Threats to validity}

%% trace: threats / scope-discipline
**Origin-classification blind spots.** edit-provenance is a debounced heuristic (typed vs AI-injected vs pasted); rapid interleaving can misattribute a burst - the agent-leg correlation strengthens but does not eliminate this (FR-INST-10, FR-AGENT-3).

%% trace: threats / scope-discipline
**Small-n framing.** pilot samples are hypothesis-generating; exact nonparametric tests and effect sizes are reported with per-cell n, and no claim rests on a bare p-value (NFR-8).

%% trace: threats / scope-discipline
**Single-IDE, single-agent scope.** capture is VS Code + Claude Code; generality to other editors/agents is by design, not demonstration (scope discipline; FR-AGENT-4 extension point).

%% trace: threats / scope-discipline
**Self-report instruments.** fatigue and stuck probes are Likert self-reports subject to the usual response biases.
